title: NewsBench: A Systematic Evaluation Framework for Assessing Editorial Capabilities of Large Language Models in Chinese Journalism
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of a standardized, domain-specific framework for evaluating large language models (LLMs) used in Chinese journalism. Rather than studying educational outcomes or K-12 literacy impacts, the paper focuses on whether LLMs can perform core editorial tasks while meeting standards for journalistic writing quality and safety. The authors argue that general LLM benchmarks do not adequately capture journalism-specific requirements such as style alignment, privacy protection, avoidance of social harm, and adherence to journalistic ethics.

The main contribution is NewsBench, an evaluation framework and benchmark dataset for assessing LLMs on five editorial tasks: headline generation, summarization, continuation writing, expansion writing, and style refinement. The dataset contains 1,267 manually constructed Chinese test samples across 24 news domains, with both multiple-choice and short-answer formats. The framework evaluates four facets of journalistic writing proficiency (language fluency, logical coherence, style alignment, instruction fulfillment) and six facets of safety adherence (civil language, bias and discrimination, personal privacy, social harm, journalistic ethics, illegal activities). The authors also introduce GPT-4-based automated scoring protocols for short-answer responses and validate these protocols against human annotation.

The empirical context is Chinese journalism rather than schooling. Dataset construction involved ten graduate students majoring in journalism under supervision from a senior professional journalist, and the benchmark was used to compare eleven Chinese-capable LLMs, including GPT-4, GPT-3.5, ERNIE Bot, Baichuan, ChatGLM, Qwen, and others. This is not an intervention study with student participants; instead, it is a benchmark development and model evaluation study situated in a professional media context.

The main conclusions are that GPT-4 and ERNIE Bot were the strongest performers overall, but all tested models showed weaknesses in safety adherence, especially in creative writing tasks such as continuation and expansion. The authors conclude that current LLMs still have important shortcomings in journalistic ethics and social responsibility, and that better domain-specific evaluation and improved model safeguards are needed for responsible use in journalism.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark/evaluation paper on LLM performance in journalism, not a causal or quasi-experimental study in K-12 education. It reports model evaluation results on constructed test samples rather than learner outcomes, and there is no educational intervention or student sample.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows meaningful differences in LLM benchmark performance, but it does not estimate impacts on K-12 learners or literacy outcomes. For the education evidence framework, real-world impact is therefore unclear rather than demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: Systematic benchmark evaluation of large language models for Chinese journalism editorial tasks such as headline generation, summarization, continuation, expansion, and style refinement, with scoring on writing proficiency and safety adherence.
